$comment: The pin-site registry (HARNESS-067, #902). It declares WHERE a model id is
pinned for ROUTING outside harness/model-map.json, and how that site spells
it, so a guard can check the two agree.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. model-map.json has a schema, a validating loader and
real compile-time consumers, and it binds no leaf. A model id is pinned in
roughly seven live places and nothing makes any of them agree with the map.
Measured 2026-08-26: ~/.pi/agent/settings.json carried
`nan/deepseek-v4-flash-0731`, which no longer resolves — pi printed
`No models match pattern` on EVERY start — plus three `openrouter/*` entries
for a provider retired in August 2026. Nobody noticed until an unrelated
investigation happened to read the file.
CATALOG IS NOT ROUTING, and the distinction is the whole design. A leaf may
OFFER models the map does not route: `qwen3.8-flash` and `glm5.3-flash` are
in pi's and opencode's pickers deliberately and deliberately absent from the
map — availability on a promotional allocation pending a community vote
(#1244). A guard reading `leaf offers what the map does not know` as drift
would fire on a recorded decision. So only the pins listed here are checked,
each one a place that DECIDES WHICH MODEL DOES WORK, and a catalog superset
is never drift.
NORMALIZATION IS DECLARED, NEVER INFERRED. One model, three correct
spellings: `nan:mimo-v2.6-flash` here, `openai/mimo-v2.6-flash` in .pr_agent.toml
(litellm treats NaN as an OpenAI-compatible provider, so the prefix names a
wire protocol rather than a vendor), and bare `mimo-v2.6-flash` in
harness/reviewer-pool.json. A grep-shaped guard cannot check that. Each entry below
carries the rule for turning its own spelling into a map-resolvable
`pool:id`.
ALIASES ARE NOT DRIFT. model-map.json pins `opus`/`sonnet`/`haiku` for claude
because Claude Code resolves those to the current member of each family, so
rotation costs nothing there; every other pool takes a canonical id. A check
demanding canonical ids uniformly would break that asymmetry, which is why
resolution is against what the map declares rather than against a pattern.
NOT LISTED, and each absence is a decision:
harness/reviewer-pool.json  separate from the map BY DECISION (its own
$comment). Its `agy/gemini-3.1-pro-high` entry
is unroutable today — a question about the
map's completeness, filed as #1253.
cli/internal/agent/backends.go  Go rather than JSON on purpose.
HIVE_EMBED_BASE_URL         an endpoint, not a model id (#1231).
ai/agy/settings.json        `modelConfigs.defaultModel` is not read by agy: the
binary carries no `modelConfigs` string, and its log
resolves `model` instead. Recorded under `excluded`.
$HOME/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json, $HOME/.claude/settings.json,
$HOME/.copilot/settings.json  the deployed copies of three repo sites below.
Not declared yet: agy's picker rewrites `model` at
runtime (measured 2026-10-01 at `Gemini 3.8 Flash
(High)`, which the map does not route), so declaring
it would fail doctor on a choice the user made in
the UI. That is a routing decision, not a registry one.
Fields:
file      repo-relative path, or a `$HOME`-rooted one for a deployed file
(never a literal home — ADR-025).
scope     `repo` (committed, checkable in CI) or `deployed` (machine
state, checkable only by dotf doctor — CI never sees a machine).
pins      each routing pin: how to find it and how to normalize it.
id      stable name for the pin, used in diagnostics.
kind    `json-path` (dotted object keys, `*` for every key at one
level, `[]` at the end for a string array), `toml-key` (`key`,
or `key[]` for a list), `regex` (exactly one match) or `regex-all` (every
match must resolve). Both regex kinds need exactly one capture
group, and both ERROR when the locator matches nothing: a
pattern that has rotted reports zero values, and zero values
check clean.
locator the path/key/pattern that extracts the raw value.
prefix  the site's provider prefix, stripped and replaced by `pool`.
An empty string means the site writes a bare id. REQUIRED when
declared: a value without it fails as misspelled rather than
resolving (round-1 finding 4).
suffix  a trailing spelling the site adds, required the same way
(`[1m]`, Claude Code's 1M-context form of an alias).
spelling  `display-name` when the site writes a picker label rather
than an id (`Gemini 3.7 Flash (High)` is `gemini-3.7-flash-high`).
catalog `true` for a picker list: checked only for ids that cannot
resolve at all, never for being a superset of the map. Declared,
not inferred from `[]`: `fallback_models` is a list AND routing.
pool    the model-map pool the normalized id must resolve in.
why       what this pin decides. A pin nobody can justify is one to delete.
excluded    routing-shaped keys that are deliberately not pins, each with a
why. The coverage sweep in model_pins_coverage_test.go reads every
routing-shaped key under ai/ and fails on one that is neither.

excluded.why: Not read by agy. Measured 2026-10-01: the agy binary carries no `modelConfigs` string, its log resolves the top-level `model`, and `gemini-3.7-flash` is not an id `agy models` lists. A leftover of the gemini-cli schema; ai/agy/AGY.md still calls it the source of truth.

sites.why: pi's interactive default — the model a bare `pi` session runs on. NOTE this file is seed-if-missing (#754): it is checked, and it will never be generated, because pi rewrites it at runtime and a rendered copy would reach a fresh machine and never an existing one.

pins.why: `deepseek-v4-flash`, the map's `tiers.mid.nan`, so it no longer diverges from the map. It was `qwen3.6` until #1255 and `qwen3.8-flash` until #1471 moved it here on 2026-09-04, in a change about subagent dispatch that recorded no reason for the model.

sites.why: The live file pi actually reads. It is the one surface the repo cannot converge, so it is the one that drifted: measured 2026-08-26 carrying a dead dated id and three retired-provider entries.

pins.why: The default a real session runs on. It must be a model the map routes: a live but unrouted id fails too, as qwen3.8-flash did once AI-044 unrouted it.
The picker catalog. Checked ONLY for ids that cannot resolve at all (a dead dated stamp, a retired provider) — never for being a superset of the map, which is what #1244 makes legitimate.

sites.why: The CI reviewer. Read from the repository by the workflow, so it can be checked and must never be rendered.

pins.why: The model every PR review runs on. The `openai/` prefix is litellm's protocol name for NaN, not a vendor — the single clearest case for declaring normalization instead of guessing it.
The cheap model for mechanical sub-tasks.
The model that reviews a PR when the primary is exhausted or dead. A list and routing at once: every entry decides who reviews, so every entry must resolve (round-1 finding 2).

sites.why: The daily-driver TUI's default. Owned by the deploy pipeline, so this is the first surface generation should claim in phase 2.

pins.why: Session titles and other light calls, on every session.
The NaN provider's own default, sent when a request names no model.
Each agent override's model (`plan` today). A wildcard, so an agent added later is checked without a registry edit; one that sets no model inherits the default and is skipped.

sites.why: Claude Code's main and advisor models, deployed to ~/.claude/settings.json.

pins.why: The model every Claude Code session opens on. `opus[1m]` is the opus alias with the 1M-token context window; the map routes the alias, so the suffix is spelling.
The reviewer model the advisor tool consults. Routed as `services.advisor`: a role pinned to one model, which no tier describes.
The model a Copilot CLI session opens on: the seat default, `tiers.mid.copilot`.

sites.why: agy's seed settings, merged into ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json. agy owns the keys it writes there (#1414), so this is the value a fresh machine starts on.

pins.why: The model agy resolves at start (its log reads `Resolving model Gemini 3.8 Flash (High)`, the deployed value). Written as the picker label, so the rule is declared: `Gemini 3.8 Flash (High)` is `gemini-3.8-flash-high`.

sites.why: The qq/qf one-shot wrappers. Three copies of the same two pins exist across shells, which is itself the drift this registry makes visible.
The bash twins of the two wrappers above. Kept in sync by hand today.

pins.why: Must agree with qq-zsh; nothing enforces that today.
Must agree with qf-zsh; nothing enforces that today.

sites.why: The Windows twins. A third copy of the same two pins, and the one least likely to be noticed when the other two are edited — the Linux-only verification loop cannot see it, the same gap GOOS=windows vet exists to close for Go.

pins.why: Both wrappers invoke the same form, so EVERY match must resolve rather than one regex per wrapper. Deliberate: a pattern clever enough to tell qq from qf across a multi-line PowerShell function is a pattern that silently matches nothing after an unrelated edit — and a locator that matches nothing is indistinguishable from a site with no drift. `regex-all` fails when there are zero matches, so it cannot pass vacuously.
